children: The Indian rupee opened lower against the US dollar on September 21, with traders watching oil prices and foreign portfolio flows for directional cues while holding on to expectations that central bank intervention will limit the currency's weakness.
The rupee opened 5 paise higher at 95.82 per dollar, compared with Friday’s close of 95.87.

According to Finrex, the Indian rupee is expected to open unchanged today as RBI does not seem to be in a mood to allow 96.00 to be breached while Brent oil prices were lower from Friday as markets focused on US-Iran diplomatic efforts even as fresh attacks by Houthi’s kept tensions elevated.
Dollar index was stable at 100.22 while Asian currencies were generally range bound this morning.

Exporters to keep selling near to 96.00 levels while importers to buy all the dips. There are 20 IPOs that would be opening for subscription this week while 14 companies including NSE and Hero Motors will get listed, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the South Korean won rising 0.194%, followed by the Taiwan dollar (0.157%), Chinese renminbi (0.13%), Malaysian ringgit (0.059%), Japanese yen (0.045%), Singapore dollar (0.024%) and Thai baht (0.015%). Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah declined 0.028% and the Philippine peso slipped 0.016%.
The dollar was quoted in a tight range against Group-of-10 peers in early trading into a week that includes leaders’ meetings during the United Nations General Assembly.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens marginally higher at 95.82 per dollar; Asian peers mixed
